title: QBR - Cobalt, Inc. - Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost spikes on long-context generation, reliability incidents in Feb, and roadmap alignment for Dedicated/Private options. Agreed next steps: share detailed cost breakdown, schedule technical deep-dive for latency benchmarks, and follow up on VPC peering timing.
action_items: Sophie Liang: prepare Q1 usage and cost spreadsheet and send by 2026-03-06
Anika Patel: run baseline latency benchmark for Cobalt's 512-token and 2048-token workloads and share results by 2026-03-12
Marco Reyes: pull reliability incident logs and SLO drift chart and share by 2026-03-05
Priya Rao: confirm VPC peering maintenance window and provide infra contact by 2026-03-05
next_steps: Send Q1 usage and cost breakdown by 2026-03-06
Share Private deployment checklist and SSO integration doc
Schedule technical deep-dive for latency benchmarks week of 2026-03-15
Provide estimate for Dedicated reservation sizing by 2026-03-10
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Marco (CSM), Anika (SE), Jared (VP ML), Priya (Head of DevOps), Liam (PM)

[00:00] Sophie Liang: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR for Cobalt, appreciate you making time. We're going to run through usage, cost, reliability, and then roadmap alignment. Marco, do you want to kick with adoption highlights?
[00:30] Marco Reyes: Yeah, quick high level. Overall tokens up 28% QoQ, most of that coming from the new summarize pipeline Jared's team rolled out in Jan. Embedding calls are stable but inferencing / generation has increased notably, especially long-context completion jobs.
[01:15] Jared Kim: Yeah, that aligns with what we saw, the summarizer runs at 1k tokens pre and then we do a 2k consolidation pass, so there's a lot of variable sequence lengths. Cost was kind of expected, but Feb had a few spikes.
[02:05] Anika Patel: On the spikes - we flagged three incidents where retry storms hit and you had requests routed to the fallback larger model. The routing policy defaulted to model-variant-b which is higher cost. We captured traces, and Marco will share.
[02:40] Priya Rao: Right, the retries were from our batcher script, we had a backoff misconfiguration after a network flake during our nightly job. Sorry about that. We fixed the backoff but want to understand how Redwood's autoscaling and fallback behaved.
[03:20] Marco Reyes: We'll share the incident timeline. In short: 02/18 03:12 UTC network flake -> 03 retries -> fallback to model-variant-b -> higher token count and latency, autoscaler scaled up but exceeded your budgeted burst so cost went up.
[04:05] Liam O'Neill: Could you remind us - what's the exact difference between the hosted route and Dedicated? We got a bit lost when we last spoke.
[04:30] Sophie Liang: Sure - hosted is our managed API, quickest on-boarding and pay-as-you-go. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and cost control. Private is the VPC/on-prem option for compliance. For you, given the budget concerns and compliance needs, Dedicated or Private are the two options to discuss.
[05:10] Jared Kim: We're leaning Dedicated to start, but curious about when moving to Private actually buys us cost wins vs just Dedicated.
[05:35] Anika Patel: Good question. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reduced per-token cost with reserved capacity; Private gives you network isolation, but the ops overhead and infra cost can offset token price unless you have sustained high throughput. Also quantization and kernel tuning matter a lot for long contexts - we can recommend profiles.
[06:10] Priya Rao: On the network side, Private VPC peering looks fine but we need a maintenance window for peering. I'll confirm dates after this call.
[06:45] Marco Reyes: Also worth highlighting: we've got intelligent KV-cache previews that could reduce your repeated prefix cost on the consolidation pipeline. If you can keep prefixes more stable we can hit better cache hit rates.
[07:20] Jared Kim: That may help. Our summarizer always sends the same intro prompt, so caching would be valuable.
[07:55] Sophie Liang: We'll run a quick analysis for your top 20 prompt patterns and show theoretical savings.
[08:30] Anika Patel: Back to reliability - March SLOs: your latency p95 slipped from 420ms to 820ms during incident windows. We had a couple of bursts that saturated the batcher. We suggest adjusting your client-side concurrency and enabling prefix caching to smooth that.
[09:10] Priya Rao: Is there a recommended client concurrency per VM? We're using 16 threads for the summarizer job.
[09:30] Anika Patel: For your 8k tokens combined flow, we usually recommend 4 concurrent in-flight requests per worker to avoid batcher starvation. We'll include a recommended tuning doc.
[10:05] Liam O'Neill: Are there any changes on the roadmap that might affect us? Anything that could improve long-context handling?
[10:30] Sophie Liang: Yes - upcoming runtime improvements this quarter include a new kernel selection path that improves memory efficiency for >4k contexts and better KV cache compaction. We're targeting alpha in April.
[11:05] Jared Kim: Nice. Do we have any guarantees on when that's GA?
[11:20] Sophie Liang: Not GA yet, but we'll give you early access for benchmarking if you'd like.
[11:40] Priya Rao: We'll take early access for sure. Could help our capacity planning.
[12:05] Marco Reyes: On costs - here's a quick breakdown I have: compute is 62% of your spend, embeddings 18%, storage and logs the rest. The Feb spike added ~14% one-time increase due to fallback model and retries.
[12:45] Jared Kim: Okay, so compute is the big lever. How much would Dedicated lower our unit costs? Ballpark.
[13:10] Anika Patel: With a 6-12 month commit, Dedicated can lower your per-token compute costs ~20-35% depending on utilization and reservation sizing. We'll do a reservation sizing exercise based on your 95th percentile throughput.
[13:50] Priya Rao: One concern: SSO and audit log integrations. We need SOC2-level logs forwarded to our SIEM. What's Redwood's support for that in Dedicated vs Private?
[14:15] Sophie Liang: Both Dedicated and Private support audit logs and KMS integrations. Private gives you control over the KMS and network egress. Dedicated has audit hooks to forward logs to your SIEM via secured event sinks. We'll share the integration guide and our SOC2 docs.
[14:50] Priya Rao: Great. Also, does Redwood support SAML with attribute mappings?
[15:05] Marco Reyes: Yes, SAML SSO with SCIM user provisioning, and we support custom attribute mapping for role-based access control. We'll include the SSO checklist.
[15:40] Liam O'Neill: On the security review front, we have a legal review coming mid-March; could you send the compliance pack and the Data Processing Addendum?
[16:00] Sophie Liang: I'll send the compliance pack and DPA after this call - expect it in the next 24 hours.
[16:20] Jared Kim: Thanks. For the dedicated sizing exercise - what data do you need from us?
[16:35] Anika Patel: We'll need 1) 14 days of per-minute p95/p50 latency and QPS for the summarizer and consolidation pipeline, 2) typical sequence length distribution, 3) preferred availability window for maintenance. Marco will send a template.
[17:10] Priya Rao: I can pull the metrics; our infra lead will help. We'll get that to you by EOD Mar 5.
[17:35] Marco Reyes: Awesome. We'll also include a sample reservation estimate and ROI calc once we have the 95th percentile throughput.
[18:05] Sophie Liang: A couple of smaller items - we've seen a few dropped telemetry samples due to rate limiting in your agent. Could you confirm the SDK version?
[18:30] Jared Kim: We're on sdk-js 1.4.2. Is that too old?
[18:45] Anika Patel: There's a patch in 1.5.x that reduces heartbeat telemetry overhead; we'll link that.
[19:10] Priya Rao: We'll schedule an update.
[19:40] Liam O'Neill: Any competitor intel worth noting? We are doing some benchmarking against Anthropic's Claude and a light in-house runner.
[20:00] Sophie Liang: Noted. In our experience Anthropic's pricing and latency profile differs on long-context jobs; we can include comparison notes but recommend focusing on throughput and ops cost rather than raw per-token when doing the ROI.
[20:30] Marco Reyes: Also we'll share a side-by-side of Dedicated vs Private economics for your traffic shape.
[21:05] Jared Kim: For the technical deep-dive, can Anika run the 512 and 2048 token scenarios and include traces so we can compare to our in-house metrics?
[21:30] Anika Patel: Yes, I'll run those and include flamegraphs and KV cache hit rate charts. Expect results by Mar 12.
[22:05] Priya Rao: About the peering window - I think we can do Mar 11 02:00-04:00 UTC. I'll confirm with infra.
[22:30] Marco Reyes: Great - we'll note that as tentative.
[23:00] Sophie Liang: Let's recap - action items: Sophie to send compliance pack and cost spreadsheet; Anika to run latency benchmarks; Marco to share incident timeline and reservation template; Priya to confirm peering window and infra contact. Any other items?
[23:40] Jared Kim: Can you also include an estimated cost delta if we enabled prefix KV caching across top-20 prompts? That was mentioned earlier.
[24:00] Anika Patel: Yes, we'll do a savings projection based on your logs.
[24:20] Liam O'Neill: One more question - does Redwood support customer-controlled key rotation cadence on Private?
[24:40] Sophie Liang: Yes, with Private you can manage KMS and rotation policies; Dedicated supports BYOK via KMS integrations but rotation is coordinated with Redwood ops. We'll lay out the differences in the doc.
[25:10] Priya Rao: Sounds good. 
[25:30] Marco Reyes: Anything else from the Redwood side?
[25:40] Sophie Liang: No, just that we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
[26:00] Jared Kim: Thanks, appreciate it.
[26:10] Priya Rao: Thanks.
[26:20] Liam O'Neill: Thanks, bye.

End summary and notes: The call ran ~26 minutes of discussion and then some wrap - total calendar slot 45 minutes. Key takeaways: compute drive spend, retry/fallback incident caused Feb spike, Dedicated looks promising for cost predictability, Private is an option if they want full network/KMS control. Next steps documented as action items.
